en: Taal Volcano in Batangas is recognized as one of the smallest active volcanoes in the world.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest and largest river in the Philippines by volume.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, situated southeast of Metro Manila.
The Philippine eagle is a rare bird of prey endemic to the forests of Mindanao and Leyte.
The rare waling-waling orchid grows naturally as an epiphyte on tall trees in the forests of Mindanao.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected marine sanctuary known for its coral biodiversity.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon that brings dry weather to the Philippines between November and April.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Palawan is the longest island province in the Philippines, stretching between the South China Sea and the Sulu Sea.
The tamaraw is a small, endangered, hoofed mammal found exclusively in the wild on the island of Mindoro.
